docs.titre: Daily activities and telling the time
docs.contenu:
🎯 Objectives
- I can talk about my day: wake up, go to school, do homework.
- I can tell the time: seven o'clock, half past eight.

🔍 Warm-up
Mime my day! The teacher mimes: sleeping, washing the face, eating breakfast. Guess the action! Then make a big clock with your arms.

📘 New words & structures
Daily actions: wake up, get up, wash my face, have breakfast, go to school, have lunch, do my homework, play, have dinner, go to bed.
Time:
- What time is it? It is seven o'clock. (7:00)
- It is half past seven. (7:30)
Structures:
- I get up at seven o'clock.
- I go to school at eight o'clock.
- I do my homework in the evening.

✏️ Practice examples
1. I wake up at seven o'clock. I wash my face and have breakfast.
2. I go to school at eight o'clock.
3. At half past twelve, I have lunch.
4. In the evening, I do my homework and go to bed at nine o'clock.

🛠️ How to say it
To tell your day:
1. Say the action: I get up...
2. Add the time with AT: ...at seven o'clock.
3. Use time words: in the morning, in the evening, at night.

⭐ Remember
- 7:00 = seven o'clock. 7:30 = half past seven.
- Use AT with time: at eight o'clock.
- First I wake up, then I get up!

🔗 Try at home
Draw three clocks: your wake-up time, your school time and your bed time. Under each clock, write one sentence: I ... at ... o'clock.

🎲 Fun corner
Human clock! Make a big clock with your arms: arms up is twelve o'clock. Your friend guesses the time. Mini-dialogue:
- What time is it?
- It is half past seven. Hurry up!
- Oh no! School is at eight o'clock!

📋 Summary
We talk about the day with actions like wake up, get up, wash my face, have breakfast, go to school, have lunch, do my homework, play, have dinner and go to bed, in that order. To tell the time we ask What time is it? and answer with o'clock for the exact hour (seven o'clock = 7:00) or half past for thirty minutes later (half past seven = 7:30). We use AT with a time: I get up at seven o'clock, I go to school at eight o'clock. Draw three clocks for your own day and write a sentence for each!
